arrive.text: A room in black and white. You have never been outside it.

scientist.text: You're a scientist. You know everything there is to know about colour: the light, the eye, the brain. Every physical fact.

tomato.text: A ripe tomato, on a black and white screen. You know exactly what happens in someone's brain when they see one.

books_1.text: Light at about seven hundred nanometres. The long-wave cones in the eye fire, and the signal runs to the back of the brain. You know every step.

books_2.text: What people say when they see it: red. Warm. Like a stop sign. You've read every word they've ever written.

board.text: The whole spectrum, drawn in chalk. In shades of grey.

desk_early.text: Not yet. There's still more to read. There always is.

ask.text: When you step outside and see red for the first time, will you learn anything new?

banana.text: A blue banana. Someone's idea of a trick. Would all your books have told you that it's blue?

learn_1.text: So that's what red is like.

learn_2.text: You knew every fact about seeing red. And still, this is new. Is it a new fact? Or only a new way of knowing an old one?

stay_1.text: You close the door, and go back to your books.

stay_2.text: You know everything there is to know about red. Maybe that's all there is to it. Maybe not.
